name: SSH commit signing (hardware-backed key, e.g. Yubikey sk-ssh)
description: Wires up git SSH commit signing for a hardware-backed key such as a Yubikey sk-ssh-ed25519 resident key. Reads the PUBLIC key (not secret) from a runtime env var — picked up automatically via an --env-file in runArgs, no shell-sourcing required — writes it into ~/.ssh, and points git config at it. Reasserts the git config on every attach, since VS Code re-copies ~/.gitconfig from the host on each connect and would otherwise clobber the path with a host-only one that doesn't exist in the container. Actual signing happens through your host's ssh-agent via VS Code's automatic agent-forwarding socket — you must `ssh-add` the private key on the HOST yourself (e.g. `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_sk`); this feature only wires the container side.

pubkeyEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the PUBLIC signing key, read at attach time. A public key is not a secret; it is read from the environment rather than baked in so the same image works for any user.

keyFilename.description: Filename written under ~/.ssh for the public key that git is pointed at.

signAllCommits.description: Set commit.gpgsign=true, so every commit is signed without passing -S. Turn off to wire up the key but sign only on demand.
